claims.claim: Reviewers state that enemy and teammate positions are not marked on the interface, requiring players to visually identify uniforms and rely heavily on communication.

citations.review_text: Good game if you're up to the challenge, there is quite a steep learning curve when you play SQUAD. If you do not like steep learning curves, then do not get this game. Communication is key within playing, and you need to be on high alert when surrounded by other players, enemies are not marked nor are your teammates. Overall, the game is good but is quite difficult.

Unique game. They seem to do many things right.
E.g.
- the suppresion mechanics degrading vision and aim;
- enemy markers are placed deliberately on the map / there is no just marking enemies with binoculars like in wardogs, so using concealment is still possible in this game here
- weapons have recoil, and you can't just sprint-shoot; you have to stabilize your aim to shoot accurately; quite frankly the button to focus aim is the same button as run - if you use directional buttons with it then you run and not aim, and if you press it without directional buttons then you aim and not run; quite genius actually and makes absolute sense
- the 'PvP wiggle' is severely reduced (i.e. that moving left and right rapidly in pvp shooter games that people do to reduce chance of being shot at accurately), so shooting mechanics are way more realistic
- guns pack a punch and look good - audio visuals are A-OK.,
- it may be unclear to you who is friend and who is a foe, because you only recognize peers at close ranges, otherwise they are not marked, so you have to suss it out, read the situation, and stay your fire before you decide to shoot or not to shoot. 
- getting revived doesn't mean you're automatically fully well - you're at a near-death state still for a while after, where your vision/functioning is impaired
etc etc.

Though

The mechanic of magically stripping you of loadout if you're not part of some squad voice chat, or you leave it, or the leader disconnects... is so incredibly punishing and non-immersive - what were the developers even thinking?!

I spent like 4 consecutive runs back and forth to re-pick up loadout from the base, and return to the front lines, over and over, because of the game's insistence we have to be on voice chats at all times.

If devs want to punish leavers somehow - create some comms interference thereafter; where the player is cut off from seeing the map, until they reestablish communications by joining another squad for example.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the server browser UI as flawed, noting problems such as an automatic refresh feature that constantly moves the list, missing refresh buttons, and details being obscured by pop-up windows.

citations.review_text:
The gameplay is great, when the game works and there are decent squad leaders stepping up.


I came back after awhile to play.

The new UI feels prettier, but there are obvious flaws. If I select a server, a new window opens up with selected server details, but it covers up the entire right side of the server browser and blurs important information on other servers (notably/importantly for me: ping) with very much wasted space, which hurts the browsing experience.
The automatic refresh constantly (every 7 seconds or so) hops the entire server list, which is really annoying, when I wanted to click something in the list. And I think the constant updating and me scanning this hopping list is hurting my eyes. Again, hurts the browsing experience.

There aren't any EU servers to play in as an English speaker during the off-hours. Sry, but I'm a player that does other things during the on-hours. 

I joined a server to seed it, then tried to queue in an American server. The game got stuck so nothing responded, not the Esc button or the "leave queue" on the server I queued in. I had to alt+F4 out of the game.

I'm beginning to understand why so many old veteran players view this game with animosity, because it feels like it's getting worse with time, thanks to all the old bugs still being present on top of the new ones and questionable development decisions (like the new UI described before and the automatic server list refresh).

I'm on the verge of uninstalling. I will probably be back to check the next couple of updates, but I think I will be done after that, if there are no meaningful improvements.
Where my refresh button at tho 😫
Can't even play this game, there's no server refresh button so you're stuck looking at an empty screen if your internet doesn't load them.

Something Oceania players should know before buying is that the population can make the game borderline unplayable. 

Servers need to be basically full (100 players) for the game to be enjoyable and since WarDogs' release the player base currently only supports one server each night. This has led to a serious problem where it can be impossible to join the only playable server for multiple hours due to:
1. The queue being 20 people long.
2. The queue being capped at 20 people (you can't join the queue if it is full).
3. Priority queue making wait times longer.

Prior to WarDogs release the population was large enough to support 2-4 servers on weekends and 1-2 servers on week days. So the game is worth buying if the population recovers.

This might sound like an ad for WarDogs, but no other mil-sim really compares to Squad. Squad forces player to participate in team work through its squad system (9 players a squad with one acting as leader) this does lead to gameplay which you will find in no other game, so I think it is worth at least trying to see if you prefer it over other options.

Vehicles are fairly balanced and most factions are viable (although not all divisons are well balanced for certain maps). However, this balance issue only affects servers that have faction/map voting at the end of rounds. 

Having a microphone is an absolute MUST to play this game. Communication is the key to teamwork and teamwork is the key to victory in Squad. The Squad leaders greatest weapon isnt the ability to build or call in a rally point to spawn allies, it relies in is connection to command chat that allows him to communicate with other squad leaders and call in support. Dont worry about being uncomfortable on the mic - Squads community is very welcoming and friendly.

Great game with a big learning curve for people coming from arcade shooters. 
Mic and communication is key, once you find a good squad that works together this game is the best.

My favourite first person shooter. Sometimes can be a highly frustrating experience, but when Squad is at its best it has some of the greatest gaming moments that you can't get anywhere else. Expect to use your mic and be asked to follow order and communicate, this is not a game for lone wolfing.
